# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Nel_2026_ceftriaxone"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Nel_2026_ceftriaxone"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.01081-25> (open access, PMC12777559)
* Supplement: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.01081-25> (Table S1, exclusion
  criteria; Figures S1-S4, goodness of fit, VPCs, observed profiles and
  first-dose-to-steady-state simulations). The supplement contains no
  additional parameter values.

Nel 2026 compared a single 2 g subcutaneous (SC) infusion of ceftriaxone with
the patients' own 2 g intravenous (IV) dose in a self-controlled cross-over
study, and fitted a two-compartment population PK model to capillary dried
blood spot (DBS) concentrations from both routes. The SC dose (in 50 mL normal
saline) was gravity-fed into the abdominal wall over about 30 minutes and
enters a depot compartment with bioavailability `F_SC` and first-order
absorption `KA_SC` (Figure 1 of the paper).

# Population

Twenty clinically stable adult inpatients at Fiona Stanley Hospital, Western
Australia, who were already receiving IV ceftriaxone 2 g completed both routes
(22 recruited, 2 withdrew before the SC dose). Fourteen (70%) were male; the
median age was 63.5 years (IQR 43.5-76.5), weight 84.5 kg (IQR 74.3-97.8),
BMI 26.9 kg/m^2, hematocrit 37.5%, serum creatinine 78 umol/L and
Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance 108 mL/min (IQR 71-147). Infections were
mainly genito-urinary (30%) and intra-abdominal (30%). Nineteen received 2 g
once daily and one 2 g every 12 h (Table 1 and Results). In total 212 DBS
concentrations were modelled.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Nel_2026_ceftriaxone")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL at CrCl 100 mL/min) | log(1.57) L/h | Table 2 'CL, l.h-1.(100 mL/min)-1'; Results 'CL = 1.57 x CrCl/100' |
| `lvc` (Vc at 70 kg, 60 years) | log(17.6) L | Table 2 'Vc, l.70kg-1 for a 60 years old' |
| `e_age_vc` | 0.0094 /year | Table 2 'thetaAGE where Vc x EXP(thetaAGE*(AGE-60))' |
| `lvp` (Vp at 70 kg) | log(12.9) L | Table 2 'VP, l.70kg-1' |
| `lq` (Q at 70 kg) | log(0.917) L/h | Table 2 'Q, l.h-1.70kg-1' |
| `lfdepot` (F_SC) | log(0.958) | Table 2 'FSC' |
| `lka` (KA_SC) | log(0.764) 1/h | Table 2 'KASC, h-1' |
| `e_crcl_cl` | 1 (fixed) | Results 'CL = 1.57 x CrCl/100' (linear) |
| `e_wt_vc`, `e_wt_vp` | 1 (fixed) | Methods (a priori allometry, exponent 1 on volumes); Results equation for Vc; Table 2 units |
| `e_wt_q` | 0.75 (fixed) | Methods (a priori allometry, exponent 0.75 on clearances); Table 2 unit 'l.h-1.70kg-1' |
| `etalcl` | 0.453^2 = 0.2052 | Table 2 'IIV CL' 45.3%, reported as 100 x sqrt(variance) |
| `etalvc` | 0.24^2 = 0.0576 | Table 2 'IIV VC' 24% |
| `propSd` | 0.157 | Table 2 'Proportional error (%)' 15.7 |
| `CL = CL_pop x CRCL/100` | n/a | Results, final-model equation |
| `Vc = Vc_pop x (WT/70) x exp(0.0094 x (AGE - 60))` | n/a | Results, final-model equation |
| Depot -> central with F and KA; two-compartment disposition | n/a | Methods and Figure 1 |
| `Cu = fu / (H x rho + (1 - H)) x C_DBS` (vignette only) | n/a | Methods, 'Population pharmacokinetics modeling' |

# Unbound plasma concentration

The model predicts the **whole-blood** (DBS) concentration `Cc`. For its
target-attainment analysis the paper converts whole-blood to unbound plasma
concentration with

`Cu = fu / (H x rho + (1 - H)) x C_DBS`

at the cohort median hematocrit `H = 0.37`, taking the red-cell partitioning
ratio `rho` and the plasma unbound fraction `fu` from Page-Sharp 2016
(Antimicrob Agents Chemother 60:14-23,
<https://doi.org/10.1128/AAC.01740-15>). Nel 2026 does not print the two values
it used. Page-Sharp 2016 Table 1 reports a red-cell partitioning ratio of 0.55,
0.61 and 0.57 and plasma protein binding of 94.5%, 95.3% and 90.1% at 10, 50
and 200 mg/L. This vignette uses `rho = 0.577` (the mean of the three) and
`fu = 0.05` (binding of about 95%, the value at 10-50 mg/L). The
three-concentration mean binding (93.3%, `fu = 0.067`) would put the simulated
mean IV peak about 40% above the 6.9 mg/L of Figure 2, whereas `fu = 0.05`
reproduces it (see below), so the figure supports the higher binding.

```{r unbound-constants}
hct_sim <- 0.37 # Methods: median hematocrit used for the conversion
rho_rbc <- mean(c(0.55, 0.61, 0.57)) # Page-Sharp 2016 Table 1
fu_plasma <- 0.05 # Page-Sharp 2016 Table 1, ~95% binding at 10-50 mg/L
blood_to_unbound <- fu_plasma / (hct_sim * rho_rbc + (1 - hct_sim))
blood_to_unbound
```

# Virtual cohort

The paper simulated 1,000 patients per route "with covariates uniformly
distributed based on the demographics of the study population" but does not
give the limits. Here creatinine clearance, weight and age are drawn
uniformly over the reported interquartile ranges, 200 patients, and each
patient receives the same regimen by both routes (mirroring the self-controlled
design): 2 g every 24 h for 10 days, IV as a 30-minute infusion into `central`
and SC as a 30-minute infusion into `depot`. The paper does not state the IV
infusion duration; the 0.5 h peak of its Figure 2 IV curve indicates a
30-minute infusion.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2026)
n_sub <- 200
covs <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  CRCL = runif(n_sub, 71, 147),
  WT = runif(n_sub, 74.3, 97.8),
  AGE = runif(n_sub, 43.5, 76.5)
)

ss_start <- 216 # start of the 10th daily dose
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.25), 0.5, 2.75)))

make_route <- function(route, cmt_dose, id_offset) {
  doses <- tibble(
    time = seq(0, ss_start, by = 24),
    evid = 1L, amt = 2000, dur = 0.5, cmt = cmt_dose
  )
  obs <- tibble(
    time = ss_start + obs_times,
    evid = 0L, amt = 0, dur = 0, cmt = "central"
  )
  tidyr::crossing(covs, bind_rows(doses, obs)) |>
    mutate(id = id + id_offset, route = route) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

events <- bind_rows(
  make_route("IV", "central", 0L),
  make_route("SC", "depot", n_sub)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Nel_2026_ceftriaxone")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("route")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    tad = time - ss_start,
    Cu = Cc * blood_to_unbound
  )

# Typical-value patient at the cohort medians.
typ_cov <- data.frame(CRCL = 108, WT = 84.5, AGE = 63.5)
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
solve_typical <- function(route, cmt_dose) {
  ev <- make_route(route, cmt_dose, 0L) |>
    filter(id == 1) |>
    mutate(CRCL = typ_cov$CRCL, WT = typ_cov$WT, AGE = typ_cov$AGE)
  # A single-subject solve returns no `id` column; add it for PKNCA.
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev, keep = c("route")) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    mutate(id = 1L)
}
# One typical patient per route, solved separately (a single-subject solve
# without random effects).
sim_typ <- bind_rows(
  solve_typical("IV", "central"),
  solve_typical("SC", "depot")
) |>
  mutate(tad = time - ss_start, Cu = Cc * blood_to_unbound)
```

# Replicate Figure 2: steady-state unbound concentrations

```{r figure-2}
fig2_digitised <- tibble::tribble(
  ~route, ~tad, ~Cu,
  "IV", 0.5, 6.9,
  "IV", 24, 1.1,
  "SC", 2.75, 4.8,
  "SC", 24, 1.1
)

fig2_sim <- sim |>
  group_by(route, tad) |>
  summarise(
    mean = mean(Cu),
    lo = quantile(Cu, 0.025),
    hi = quantile(Cu, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(fig2_sim, aes(tad, mean, colour = route, fill = route)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig2_digitised, aes(tad, Cu), shape = 4, size = 3, stroke = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(IV = "black", SC = "grey45")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(IV = "black", SC = "grey45")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 6)) +
  labs(
    x = "Hours after the steady-state dose",
    y = "Unbound plasma ceftriaxone (mg/L)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 2 of Nel 2026: simulated mean and 2.5th-97.5th percentiles.",
      "Crosses: values read from the published figure."
    )
  )
```

```{r figure-2-table}
typ_cu <- sim_typ |>
  select(route, tad, typical = Cu)

fig2_cmp <- fig2_digitised |>
  left_join(
    sim |>
      group_by(route, tad) |>
      summarise(mean = mean(Cu), median = median(Cu), .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("route", "tad")
  ) |>
  left_join(typ_cu, by = c("route", "tad")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff_median = 100 * (median - Cu) / Cu)

fig2_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Route" = route,
    "Time after dose (h)" = tad,
    "Figure 2 (mg/L)" = Cu,
    "Simulated mean (mg/L)" = mean,
    "Simulated median (mg/L)" = median,
    "Typical patient (mg/L)" = typical,
    "Median vs Figure 2 (%)" = pct_diff_median
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Unbound concentration: Figure 2 versus simulation.")

peaks <- fig2_cmp |> filter(tad < 24)
stopifnot(
  # Peak height is set by the dose, Vc, F_SC, KA_SC and the unbound
  # conversion; a mis-transcribed volume or bioavailability moves it by far
  # more than this.
  all(abs(peaks$pct_diff_median) < 20)
)
```

The peaks agree with the figure: the simulated median is within about 10% of
both the IV and the SC peak, and the typical patient (cohort-median CrCl,
weight and age) gives about 6.6 and 4.8 mg/L against 6.9 and 4.8 mg/L. The simulated *mean* is higher than the
median because log-normal variability on clearance and volume skews the
distribution of concentrations to the right; the published curve sits closer
to the central tendency. The simulated trough is higher than the figure's
~1.1 mg/L by every measure. The trough is set by clearance, and the paper's
virtual cohort used covariate limits that it does not report; a cohort with
more high-CrCl patients than the interquartile range used here would bring the
trough down. This is recorded as a known deviation rather than adjusted.

# Paper claims: bioavailability, peak and trough

The paper states that SC dosing gives lower peaks and comparable troughs, and a
bioavailability of 95.8%. For the typical patient the steady-state exposure is:

```{r typical-claims}
typ_summary <- sim_typ |>
  filter(tad <= 24) |>
  group_by(route) |>
  summarise(
    cmax = max(Cc),
    tmax = tad[which.max(Cc)],
    ctrough = Cc[tad == 24],
    .groups = "drop"
  )
typ_summary |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Route" = route,
    "Cmax,ss whole blood (mg/L)" = cmax,
    "Tmax (h after start)" = tmax,
    "C24,ss whole blood (mg/L)" = ctrough
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

iv <- typ_summary[typ_summary$route == "IV", ]
sc <- typ_summary[typ_summary$route == "SC", ]
stopifnot(
  sc$cmax < 0.85 * iv$cmax, # lower SC peak
  abs(sc$ctrough / iv$ctrough - 1) < 0.10 # comparable trough
)
```

# PKNCA validation

PKNCA is run on the steady-state dosing interval of each route. Because CL is
route-independent, the ratio of steady-state AUC0-24 (SC / IV) is the absolute
SC bioavailability, and should return `F_SC = 0.958` for every patient whose
parameters are the same on both routes. The typical-value patient checks this
exactly; the stochastic cohort is summarised for Cmax, Tmax and AUC.

```{r pknca}
nca_input <- function(d) {
  # PKNCA reserves a dose column called `route`, so the grouping column is
  # renamed to `treatment` for the NCA.
  conc <- d |>
    filter(!is.na(Cc), tad >= 0, tad <= 24) |>
    select(id, treatment = route, tad, Cc)
  dose <- conc |>
    distinct(id, treatment) |>
    mutate(tad = 0, amt = 2000)
  list(conc = conc, dose = dose)
}

run_nca <- function(d) {
  x <- nca_input(d)
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(x$conc, Cc ~ tad | treatment + id)
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(x$dose, amt ~ tad | treatment + id)
  intervals <- data.frame(
    start = 0, end = 24,
    cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
  )
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
}

nca_typ <- as.data.frame(run_nca(sim_typ))
auc_typ <- nca_typ |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  select(treatment, PPORRES)
f_typ <- auc_typ$PPORRES[auc_typ$treatment == "SC"] /
  auc_typ$PPORRES[auc_typ$treatment == "IV"]
f_typ
# Same drawn parameters on both sides, so the only difference is
# trapezoidal error on a 0.25 h grid.
stopifnot(abs(f_typ - 0.958) < 0.005)

nca_pop <- run_nca(sim)
summary(nca_pop)
```

```{r pknca-stats}
nca_pop_df <- as.data.frame(nca_pop) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin", "auclast")) |>
  select(id, treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

pop_cmp <- nca_pop_df |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    cmax = median(cmax),
    cmin = median(cmin),
    auclast = median(auclast),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
pop_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Route" = treatment,
    "Median Cmax,ss (mg/L)" = cmax,
    "Median Cmin,ss (mg/L)" = cmin,
    "Median AUC0-24,ss (mg*h/L)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Steady-state whole-blood NCA by route (stochastic cohort).")

stopifnot(
  # Centre of the distribution: the SC/IV AUC ratio of the medians tracks F_SC.
  abs(pop_cmp$auclast[pop_cmp$treatment == "SC"] /
    pop_cmp$auclast[pop_cmp$treatment == "IV"] - 0.958) < 0.10,
  # SC peak below IV peak in the median.
  pop_cmp$cmax[pop_cmp$treatment == "SC"] < pop_cmp$cmax[pop_cmp$treatment == "IV"]
)
```

The paper reports no NCA table, so there is no published NCA to compare
against; the checks above use the quantities the paper does state
(bioavailability, the peak/trough comparison and Figure 2).

# Replicate Figure 3: probability of target attainment

Target attainment is unbound concentration above the MIC for more than 40% of
the 24 h dosing interval at steady state.

```{r figure-3}
mics <- 2^seq(-5, 3)
dt <- 0.25 # observation grid step (h)
pta <- sim |>
  filter(tad >= 0, tad < 24) |>
  tidyr::crossing(mic = mics) |>
  group_by(route, id, mic) |>
  summarise(ft = mean(Cu > mic), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(route, mic) |>
  summarise(pta = mean(ft > 0.4), .groups = "drop")

fig3_digitised <- tibble::tribble(
  ~mic, ~IV, ~SC,
  0.5, 0.96, 0.98,
  1, 0.86, 0.89,
  2, 0.60, 0.62,
  4, 0.23, 0.23,
  8, 0.02, 0.02
) |>
  pivot_longer(c(IV, SC), names_to = "route", values_to = "pta")

ggplot(pta, aes(mic, pta, linetype = route)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig3_digitised, shape = 4, size = 3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, colour = "grey70", linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log2", breaks = mics, labels = format(mics)) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(IV = "dashed", SC = "solid")) +
  labs(
    x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "PTA (fT > 40% MIC)", linetype = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Nel 2026. Crosses: values read from the published figure."
  )
```

```{r figure-3-table}
pta |>
  filter(mic >= 0.5) |>
  left_join(fig3_digitised |> rename(pta_pub = pta), by = c("route", "mic")) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Route" = route,
    "MIC (mg/L)" = mic,
    "Simulated PTA" = pta,
    "Figure 3 PTA" = pta_pub
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

```{r figure-3-claim}
pta_wide <- pta |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = route, values_from = pta)
# The paper's claim: SC and IV target attainment are comparable at every MIC.
stopifnot(all(abs(pta_wide$SC - pta_wide$IV) < 0.15))
```

The shape of Figure 3 is reproduced: near-complete attainment up to 0.5 mg/L,
a fall through 1-4 mg/L, near-zero attainment at 8 mg/L, and SC and IV curves
that lie on top of each other. At MICs of 1 and 2 mg/L the simulated PTA is
higher than the published one, for the same reason as the higher trough above:
the vignette's cohort, drawn over the interquartile covariate ranges, has fewer
high-clearance patients than the paper's. The model is not adjusted to match.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Whole-blood output.** `Cc` is the DBS (whole-blood) concentration the model
  was fitted to. The unbound plasma conversion is applied in this vignette, not
  in the model, because the paper treats it as a post-processing step with
  literature constants it does not print.
- **`fu` and `rho`.** Taken from Page-Sharp 2016 Table 1 (the reference the
  paper cites): `rho = 0.577` (mean of 0.55, 0.61, 0.57) and `fu = 0.05`
  (about 95% binding, the value at 10-50 mg/L). The choice of `fu` among the
  reported concentration-specific values was made by the maintainers by
  comparison with the peak of Figure 2.
- **IV infusion duration.** Not stated; 30 minutes was used, consistent with
  the 0.5 h IV peak in Figure 2. The SC infusion was given over "approximately
  30 minutes" (Methods) and is modelled as a 30-minute zero-order input into
  the depot, with `F_SC` applied to the depot.
- **Virtual cohort.** The paper's uniform covariate limits are not reported;
  CrCl, weight and age are drawn uniformly over the reported interquartile
  ranges. This narrows the clearance spread compared with the paper's cohort,
  which is the most likely reason the simulated mean trough sits above the
  ~1.1 mg/L of Figure 2.
- **Bioavailability value.** Table 2 gives `F_SC = 0.958`; the abstract and
  Results quote the bootstrap median 95.7%. The table estimate is used.
- **Allometric exponents.** Applied a priori and fixed (0.75 on clearances, 1
  on volumes, reference 70 kg). In the final model clearance carries no weight
  term (`CL = 1.57 x CrCl/100`), so the 0.75 exponent applies to Q only.
- **Figure 2 trough and Figure 3 PTA at 1-2 mg/L.** Both are higher in this
  vignette than in the paper. They depend on the clearance distribution of the
  virtual cohort, whose limits the paper does not report; peaks, which depend
  on the volume and absorption parameters, agree.
- No erratum or correction notice was found for Nel 2026 as of 2026-11-11.
